questions.module: Module Quiz 34.1: Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
questions.text: For a lessee with an operating lease, which of the following is most accurate?

options.text: Both IFRS and US GAAP report interest and amortization in the income statement.
For both IFRS and US GAAP, the right-of-use (ROU) asset will equal the lease liability over the life of the lease.
IFRS will typically result in a lower ROU asset than US GAAP.

questions.explanation: US GAAP reports an income statement expense that is equal to the lease payment. While conceptually, the amount contains both interest and amortization, they are not shown separately on the income statement. IFRS reports both interest and amortization in the income statement, and the aggregate of the two amounts will not equal the lease payment. Under US GAAP, the ROU asset and the lease liability are equal at all points over the lease’s life. Under IFRS, the only points where the ROU asset is the same as the lease liability are at initiation and the end of the lease. IFRS will result in a lower ROU asset than US GAAP. Under IFRS, the ROU asset is amortized over the life of the asset (using either straight-line or accelerated methods). Under US GAAP, the amortization is equal to the principal payment on the liability. Principal payments initially are lower due to the high interest cost, but as the lease ages and the liability decreases, the interest element of each payment will decrease and the principal element will increase. The result is that accumulated amortization under IFRS is greater than US GAAP, resulting in a lower ROU asset. (LOS 34.a)

questions.module: Module Quiz 34.1: Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
questions.text: If the lessor in a finance lease is a manufacturer or dealer of leased equipment, the lessor will:

options.text: retain the asset in its balance sheet and continue to depreciate it.
record higher revenues at lease inception when compared to an operating lease.
record lease revenue in its income statement rather than interest and amortization.

questions.explanation: Finance leases for a lessor may be classified as either sales-type leases or direct financing leases. If the lessor is a manufacturer or dealer of the leased equipment, the asset is treated as inventory sold at the outset of the lease. Revenue is reported as well as a cost of sales amount. The revenue is the present value of lease receipts. Cost of sales is the carrying value of the asset less the present value of any residual value. The lease is a direct financing lease if the lessor is a financing company (buying an asset on behalf of the lessee and leasing it out). Any gain or loss on derecognition of the asset does not affect the income statement on lease initiation. The gain or loss is deferred and recognized in the income statement, as interest, over the life of the lease. For an operating lease, revenue is recognized when lease payments from the lessee fall due. (LOS 34.a)

questions.module: Module Quiz 34.2: Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
questions.text: Which of the following is least likely a criticism of employee stock options?

options.text: The binary nature of option payoffs may encourage excessive risk taking.
The fair value requires subjective estimates at the grant date.
They result in cash outflows for the company on exercise.

questions.explanation: On exercise, the company receives the option’s exercise price (a cash inflow to the company) and creates new shares. This dilutes existing stockholders’ ownership proportions in the company. The fair value of the option at the grant date requires subjective estimation—in particular, the volatility of the company’s stock price over the service period. By nature, options have binary payoffs, being either zero if the stock price is below the exercise price or positive if the stock price is above the exercise price. This may lead to excessive risk taking because the option holder gains if the stock price increases, but if the stock price decreases the option holder does not experience losses except in the sense that the options go unexercised. (LOS 34.b)

questions.module: Module Quiz 35.1: Analysis of Income Taxes
questions.text: Which of the following is least likely to result in the creation of a deferred tax asset (DTA)?

options.text: Expenses or losses that are tax deductible before they are recognized in the income statement.
Revenues or gains that are taxable before they are recognized in the income statement.
Tax loss carryforwards that are available to reduce future taxable income.

questions.explanation: Expenses that are tax deductible before they are recognized in the income statement result in deferred tax liabilities. For example, accelerated depreciation in the tax returns versus straight-line depreciation in the accounts results in more depreciation being recognized in the tax returns, in early periods, and results in carrying value exceeding the tax base. If revenues or gains are taxable before they are recognized in the income statement, DTAs are created. Unearned revenue is a good example of this. Tax loss carryforwards result from negative taxable income. Rather than triggering the tax authorities to pay tax to the firm, they are deferred and can be offset against future taxable income. As a result, the firm will pay less tax in the future, and a DTA is created. (LOS 35.a)

questions.module: Module Quiz 35.2: Analysis of Income Taxes
questions.text: Enigma KK uses straight-line depreciation in its accounts, while using accelerated depreciation for tax purposes. For both financial and tax reporting, the company assumes a five-year useful economic life and zero residual value. In the current year, accounting depreciation is ¥10,000,000 and tax allowable depreciation is ¥8,000,000. options.text: The tax expense will be greater than tax payable.
The carrying value of the asset is greater than the tax base.

questions.explanation: The carrying value is higher than the tax base of the asset due to the use of accelerated depreciation in the tax returns versus straight-line in the accounts. questions.text: Which of the following statements about coefficient of variation is least accurate?

options.text: A coefficient of variation for an income statement measure represents variation per monetary unit.
The coefficient of variation is calculated by dividing a mean value by its standard deviation.
The coefficient of variation is a size-adjusted measure of variation.

questions.explanation: Coefficient of variation is computed by dividing standard deviation by mean; therefore, it can be interpreted as risk per monetary unit for the income statement variable considered. questions.module: Module Quiz 44.2: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) and Growth Models
questions.text: Arena Distributors currently pays no dividends. The company recently reported earnings of $1.50 per share, which an analyst expects to grow at a 15% rate for the next four years. Beginning in Year 5, the analyst expects Arena to distribute 20% of its earnings in the form of dividends, and to have a constant growth rate of 5%. Using a required rate of return of 12%, the value of Arena shares today is closest to:
questions.explanation: First, forecast the earnings in Year 5, then calculate the dividends in Year 5 as 20% of Year 5 earnings. Applying the constant growth model to the Year 5 dividend gives us an estimate of the terminal value in Year 4. The terminal value discounted back four years is the current value of the stock: E4 = $1.50 × (1.15)4 = $2.62 (earnings grow at 15% per year for four years). E5 = $2.62 × 1.05 = $2.75 (earnings grow at 5% starting in the fifth year). D5 = $2.75 × 0.20 = $0.55 (payout ratio is 20%) Because there are no dividends for the first four years, the value today is PV of the terminal value at the end of Year 4: (LOS 44.b)

questions.module: Module Quiz 46.2: Financial Statement Forecasting in Equity Valuation
questions.text: Beta Industrials has $10 million par value of debt coming due at the end of the year. Beta’s auditors have issued a qualified audit report indicating doubts about the firm’s going-concern assumption. Beta’s current annual sales are $15 million. An analyst estimates that the firm’s enterprise value-to-sales ratio is 2x as a going concern, with a 50% probability, or a liquidation enterprise value-to-sales ratio of 0.8x. The analyst’s equity valuation of Beta is closest to:
questions.explanation: Enterprise value as a going concern = $15 million × 2 = $30 million. Equity value as a going concern = enterprise value as a going concern – value of debt = $30 million – $10 million = $20 million. Enterprise value in liquidation = $15 million × 0.8 = $12 million. Equity value in liquidation = $12 million – $10 million = $2 million. Probability-weighted equity value = 0.50 × $20 million + 0.50 × $2 million = $11 million. (LOS 46.b)

questions.module: Learning Module 2 — Understanding Business Cycles
questions.text: Which one of the following trends in various economic indicators is most consistent with a recovery from a recession?

options.text: A declining inventory–sales ratio and stable industrial production index
A rising broad stock market index and unit labor costs turning from increasing to decreasing
A decrease in average weekly initial claims for unemployment insurance and an increase in aggregate real personal income

questions.explanation: C is correct. The improving leading indicator, average weekly initial claims for unemployment insurance, and the improving coincident indicator, aggregate real personal income, are most consistent with an economic recovery. Even though a declining inventory-to-sales ratio, a lagging indicator, is consistent with an early recovery, the coincident indicator, the stable industrial production index, does not support that conclusion. Although a rising stock market index can signal economic expansion, the lagging indicator, the unit labor costs, has peaked, which is more consistent with a recession.

questions.module: Learning Module 5 — Introduction to Geopolitics
questions.text: A consequence of one of the disadvantages of globalization is that:

options.text: pay differences between countries have narrowed.
emerging market trade flows have grown more important.
greater economic and financial cooperation has increased interdependence.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Through the process of greater economic and financial cooperation, companies may become dependent on other countries’ resources for their supply chains. On aggregate, this can result in the nation itself becoming dependent on other nations for certain resources (such as rare earth metals, cobalt, or copper). If there is a disruption to the supply chain, including via a moment of political non-cooperation, then firms may not be able to produce the good themselves. A is incorrect because the narrowing of pay differences between countries results from a motivation to pursue globalization, which is related to one of its advantages. It is an important way for companies to increase profitability by reducing their costs. Although wage differentials remain, they are decreasing. B is incorrect because the proportion of flows between developed economies as a share of overall trade continuing to decline as emerging market trade flows rise is a function of increased international investment. This increased investment has provided beneficial aggregate economic benefits, such as increased choice, higher quality goods, increased competition among firms, higher efficiency, and increased labor mobility.

questions.module: Learning Module 7 — Capital Flows and the FX Market
questions.text: What will be the effect on a direct exchange rate quote if the domestic currency appreciates?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In the case of a direct exchange rate, the domestic currency is the price currency (the numerator) and the foreign currency is the base currency (the denominator). If the domestic currency appreciates, then fewer units of the domestic currency are required to buy one unit of the foreign currency, and the exchange rate (domestic per foreign) declines. For example, if British pound sterling (GBP) appreciates against the euro (EUR), then euro–sterling (GBP/EUR) might decline.

questions.module: Learning Module 1 — Returns of Financial Assets and Instruments
questions.text: When analyzing investment returns, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The geometric mean will exceed the arithmetic mean for a series with non-zero variance.
The geometric mean measures an investment’s compound rate of growth over multiple periods.
The arithmetic mean measures an investment’s terminal value over multiple periods.

questions.explanation: The correct response is B. The geometric mean compounds the periodic returns of every period, giving the investor a more accurate measure of the terminal value of an investment. Alternative A is incorrect: Geometric mean will not exceed the arithmetic mean for a series with zero variance (i.e., no variability in returns) but will be the same as the arithmetic mean. Recall that the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality principle states that the difference between the arithmetic and geometric mean returns increases with the variability of the returns. If there is no variability in returns, there is no difference between the arithmetic and geometric average. Alternative C is incorrect because it is the compound growth rate and not the arithmetic mean that measures an investment’s terminal value over multiple periods.

questions.text: When evaluating investment returns, which statement is accurate?

options.text: The geometric mean is higher than the arithmetic mean when there’s variability in returns.

questions.text: A wider range of annual returns for an asset class is typically associated with:

questions.module: Learning Module 3 — Benchmarking Returns
questions.text: Stock A is included in both an equal-weighted index and a price-weighted index, with the same proportional representation in each. A two-for-one stock split for Stock A is announced and will take effect immediately before the reweighting date of both indexes. Assuming no other stocks in the indexes undergo splits and there are no significant price fluctuations or capital distributions for these stocks, the price change due to the stock split for Stock A will impact:

options.text: the price-weighted index more than the equal-weighted index.
the equal-weighted index more than the price-weighted index.

questions.explanation: The correct response is B: It will impact the price-weighted index more than the equal-weighted index. In a price-weighted index, each stock’s contribution to the index is directly proportional to its price. Therefore, when Stock A undergoes a two-for-one split and its price is halved, its influence on the index diminishes. This result makes the price-weighted index more sensitive to stock splits compared to an equal-weighted index, where each stock contributes equally regardless of price changes. Alternative A is incorrect: The impact on the price-weighted index is greater than on the equal-weighted index. Alternative C is incorrect: In an equal-weighted index, each stock contributes equally to the index’s performance, regardless of its price. A two-for-one stock split doubles the number of shares but halves the price per share. However, since each stock maintains the same weighting, the split does not alter the overall influence of the stock within the index.

questions.module: Learning Module 5 — Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
questions.text: What is the purpose of dividing data into quantiles?

options.text: To rank the data in ascending order only
To divide up data into meaningful subsets, allowing for comparison of data based on distinguishing characteristics
To calculate the average value of each data segment

questions.explanation: The correct response is B: to divide up data into meaningful subsets, allowing for comparison of data based on distinguishing characteristics. Dividing data into quantiles (such as quartiles, quintiles, or deciles) allows analysts to evaluate and compare segments of the data based on certain characteristics. For example, ranking companies by market value deciles helps in comparing the performance of small versus large companies, where size is an explanatory variable. A is incorrect: Ranking the data in ascending (or descending) order is a step in dividing data into quantiles. The primary purpose is not just to rank data but to analyze it in grouped segments. C is incorrect: Calculating the average, or any other statistical measure, for each segment is possible after dividing data into quantiles, but this is not the primary purpose of analyzing quantiles. Quantiles structure the data for comparative analysis rather than for the direct calculation of averages within segments.

questions.module: Learning Module 5 — Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
questions.text: Why is Bessel’s correction used in sample variance and standard deviation calculations?

options.text: To adjust for the underestimation of population variance and standard deviation
To increase the complexity of statistical calculations
To align with the total number of observations in the sample

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A: to adjust for the underestimation of population variance and standard deviation. Bessel’s correction addresses the tendency of a sample variance to underestimate the population variance. When estimating population parameters from a sample, using n in the denominator leads to a lower variance value compared to the true population variance. This correction accounts for the reduced degrees of freedom in a sample. B is incorrect: Bessel’s correction is applied to address a specific bias in statistical estimation with the goal of accuracy in estimation, not complexity. C is incorrect: Bessel’s correction involves adjusting the calculation to reflect the degrees of freedom in the sample, not just to align with the number of observations.

questions.module: Learning Module 5 — Statistical Characteristics of Asset Returns
questions.text: Unlike standard deviation, the mean absolute deviation:

options.text: squares each deviation from the mean, providing a measure that is more sensitive to outliers.
is calculated only for data points above the median, making it suitable for distributions that are asymmetric about the mean.
uses the values of the distances from the mean, making it less sensitive to extreme values.

questions.explanation: The correct response is C: Mean absolute deviation uses the absolute values of deviations from the mean, making it less sensitive to extreme values. Mean absolute deviation measures data variability by taking the absolute values of the differences between each data point and the mean. This approach differs from the standard deviation, which squares the deviations and then takes the square root of their average. The use of absolute values means it does not magnify outliers or extreme values as much as standard deviation does, making mean absolute deviation a robust measure of variability, especially in distributions with significant outliers. A is incorrect: This description actually applies to the standard deviation, not to the mean absolute deviation. B is incorrect: Mean absolute deviation is calculated using all data points, not just those above the median.

questions.text: Consider an asset with a mean return of 0% and an annualized standard deviation of 5%. Based on a 99% VaR with a corresponding Z-score of 2.33, the asset:

questions.explanation: The correct response is B. Using the standard deviation of 5% and the Z-score for the 99% confidence level of 2.33, we calculate 99% one-year VaR as ​VaR = Z × Standard deviation = 2.33 × 0.05 = 0.1165.​ Therefore, the correct interpretation is that the asset has a 1% chance of losing more than 11.65% in a year. A is incorrect: It misinterprets the VaR concept. VaR is a lower bound on the potential loss at a given confidence level, not a strict upper limit on losses. C is incorrect: It misinterprets VaR as a lower bound on potential gains. In fact, the opposite would be true under these assumptions: We have 99% confidence that the asset’s return would not exceed 11.65% in a year.

questions.module: Learning Module 9 — Simulation of Financial Asset Prices and Returns
questions.text: Compared to Monte Carlo simulation, which of the following is a limitation of the bootstrapping approach?

options.text: Scenarios are confined to the range of the sample set.
Computational times are in general significantly higher.

questions.explanation: B is the correct response. Limited extrapolation is a key drawback of bootstrapping: We are limited to drawing samples from the data provided. For example, if the true underlying distribution for a particular variable is a standard normal but the sample set is limited to the range −1.65 to 1.65 standard deviations, then we will never see potential outcomes from data outside that range—which we know would encompass about 10% of the observations if we were to pull directly from a standard normal distribution with a Monte Carlo simulation. A is incorrect. Bootstrapping is actually ideal for non-parametric distributions. C is incorrect. There should not be a significant increase in computational time for bootstrapping relative to Monte Carlo simulation. In fact, since bootstrapping requires fewer calculations to develop the random numbers, one might expect a well-constructed program to have less computational demands.

questions.explanation: The correct response is A. The null hypothesis states that the policy shift did not change the money supply growth rate (i.e., the coefficient on SHIFT is zero). The t-statistic for the SHIFT coefficient is −8.1618, which is beyond the critical t-values of ±2.048 at the 5% significance level. Therefore, the analyst should reject the null hypothesis and conclude that the money supply growth rate did change after the policy shift. options.text: Big data involve formats with diverse structures.
One of big data’s traditional sources is business processes.
Real-time communication of big data is uncommon due to vast content.

questions.text: In the use of machine learning:

options.text: some techniques are called “black box” due to data biases.
human judgment is not needed because algorithms continuously learn from data.
training data can be learned too precisely, resulting in inaccurate predictions when used with different datasets.

questions.explanation: The correct response is C. Overfitting occurs when the ML model learns the input and target dataset too precisely. In this case, the model has been “over-trained” on the data and is treating noise in the data as true parameters. An ML model that has been overfitted is not able to accurately predict outcomes using a different dataset. A is incorrect: ML models are called “black boxes” due to their complexity and lack of interpretability, not because of data biases. The following information relates to questions 15-21 Hans Annan, CFA, a food and beverage analyst, is reviewing Century Chocolate’s inventory policies as part of his evaluation of the company. Century Chocolate, based in Switzerland, manufactures chocolate products and purchases and resells other confectionery products to complement its chocolate line. Annan visited Century Chocolate’s manufacturing facility last year. He learned that cacao beans, imported from Brazil, represent the most significant raw material and that the work-in-progress inventory consists primarily of three items: roasted cacao beans, a thick paste produced from the beans (called chocolate liquor), and a sweetened mixture that needs to be “conched” to produce chocolate. On the tour, Annan learned that the conching process ranges from a few hours for lower-quality products to six days for the highest-quality chocolates. While there, Annan saw the facility’s climate-controlled area where manufactured finished products (cocoa and chocolate) and purchased finished goods are stored prior to shipment to customers. After touring the facility, Annan had a discussion with Century Chocolate’s CFO regarding the types of costs that were included in each inventory category. Annan has asked his assistant, Joanna Kern, to gather some preliminary information regarding Century Chocolate’s financial statements and inventories. He also asked Kern to calculate the inventory turnover ratios for Century Chocolate and another chocolate manufacturer for the most recent five years. Annan does not know Century Chocolate’s most direct competitor, so he asks Kern to do some research and select the most appropriate company for the ratio comparison. Kern reports back that Century Chocolate prepares its financial statements in accordance with IFRS. She tells Annan that the policy footnote states that raw materials and purchased finished goods are valued at purchase cost, whereas work in progress and manufactured finished goods are valued at production cost. Raw material inventories and purchased finished goods are accounted for using the FIFO method, and the weighted average cost method is used for other inventories. An allowance is established when the net realizable value of any inventory item is lower than the value calculated previously. Kern provides Annan with the selected financial statements and inventory data for Century Chocolate. The ratio exhibit Kern prepared compares Century Chocolate’s inventory turnover ratios to those of Gordon’s Goodies, a US-based company. Annan returns the exhibit and tells Kern to select a different competitor that reports using IFRS rather than US GAAP. During this initial review, Annan asks Kern why she has not indicated whether Century Chocolate uses a perpetual or a periodic inventory system. Kern replies that she learned that Century Chocolate uses a perpetual system but did not include this information in her report because inventory values would be the same under either a perpetual or periodic inventory system. Annan tells Kern she is wrong and directs her to research the matter. While Kern is revising her analysis, Annan reviews the most recent month’s Cocoa Market Review from the International Cocoa Organization. He is drawn to the statement that “the ICCO daily price, averaging prices in both futures markets, reached a 29-year high in US dollar terms and a 23-year high in special drawing rights (SDRs) terms (the SDR unit comprises a basket of major currencies used in international trade: US dollar, euro, pound sterling, and yen).” Annan makes a note that he will need to factor the potential continuation of this trend into his analysis. reviewQueue.explanation: A is correct. An inventory write-down increases the cost of sales and reduces profit and reduces the carrying value of inventory and assets. This has a negative effect on profitability and solvency ratios. However, activity ratios appear positively affected by a write-down because the asset base, whether total assets or inventory (denominator), is reduced. The numerator, sales, in total asset turnover is unchanged, and the numerator, cost of sales, in inventory turnover is increased. Thus, turnover ratios are higher and appear more favorable as the result of the write-down.

reviewQueue.module: Learning Module 11 — Financial Analysis Techniques
reviewQueue.text: Based on the data in Exhibit 1, what is the analyst least likely to conclude? A. Inventory management has contributed to improved liquidity. B. Management of payables has contributed to improved liquidity. C. Management of receivables has contributed to improved liquidity.
reviewQueue.explanation: C is correct. The analyst is unlikely to reach the conclusion given in Statement C because days of sales outstanding increased from 23 days in FY1 to 25 days in FY2 to 28 days in FY3, indicating that the time required to collect receivables has increased over the period. This is a negative factor for Spherion’s liquidity. By contrast, days of inventory on hand dropped over the period FY1 to FY3, a positive for liquidity. The company’s increase in days payable, from 35 days to 40 days, shortened its cash conversion cycle, thus also contributing to improved liquidity.
